correctness.rationale: For the male-search mechanism, conditioning on \(Y=e^{-a\sum_i T_i}\) gives \(K_M\mid Y\sim\operatorname{Bin}(n,1-Y)\); for female search, \(K_F\sim\operatorname{Bin}(n,1-q)\) with \(q=\mathbb E[e^{-naT}]\). Both zero-mating probabilities equal \(q^n\). After size-biasing by \(Y^n\), the ratios \(R_k\) of point masses are moments of a nonnegative random variable. Strict Hölder gives \(R_1<1\) for nonconstant \(T\); moment log-convexity and normalization force one negative-to-positive sign change, and thus strict upper-tail ordering at each \(2\le k\le n\). The constant-lifetime and \(n=1\) equality cases are explicit. The standalone exact-rational diagnostics passed 13,754 assertions, but the general result is established analytically.

originality.rationale: Neither the inspected Byers (2012, 2007) articles nor the indexed closest scientific findings supply the identical any-mating probability and strict all-higher-threshold order for every independent search-lifetime distribution. Observed mean trends, monogamous encounter models, and deterministic demographic equations do not imply this stronger full distribution law. Classic Laplace-transform and moment convexity are known proof tools, not claimed innovations. Residual full-text and general stochastic-order priority risks remain.

value.rationale: A natural sex-search asymmetry in trap-limited mating gives a structural distribution-free phenomenon: identical probability of any mating but strictly ordered chances of two or more mated females under heterogeneous search lifetimes. This resolves different low-count and higher-count intervention endpoints in the idealized model without calibrating a lifetime law. It is a substantive exact classification rather than a fitted table, and it exposes when an average mating comparison cannot characterize reproductive-event tails. Its application is confined to the explicit independent-contact, polygynous assumptions.
